entries.label: On-site data-center water usage effectiveness (WUE)
entries.evidence: Based on our FY25 global average WUE of 0.27 L per kWh, our owned datacenters have achieved a 25% reduction in WUE since our 2022 baseline, progressing towards our 2030 target of a 40% reduction.

entries.label: Water consumed per kWh of electricity generated (EWIF)
entries.source_title: 2024 United States Data Center Energy Usage Report (Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory)
entries.evidence: In 2023, energy consumption by a data center translates to national average of 4.52 L/kWh of indirect water consumption, along with 0.34 kg/ kWh emissions.

entries.label: Energy per median Gemini Apps text prompt (Google)
entries.source_title: Measuring the environmental impact of delivering AI at Google Scale
entries.evidence: Median Gemini Apps text prompt uses 0.24 Wh under the comprehensive boundary (0.10 Wh counting only active accelerators). Google reports a 33x drop in energy per median prompt over one year.

entries.label: Water per median Gemini Apps text prompt (Google)
entries.source_title: Measuring the environmental impact of delivering AI at Google Scale
entries.evidence: Google reports 0.26 mL of water (about five drops), 0.24 Wh and 0.03 gCO2e for the median Gemini Apps text prompt under its comprehensive serving boundary. A narrower boundary counting only active TPU/GPU use gives 0.12 mL. Counts data-center water consumption, not the water behind electricity generation. Self-reported; models not named.

entries.label: Water per 400-token Le Chat response, lifecycle (Mistral)
entries.source_title: Our contribution to a global environmental standard for AI
entries.evidence: Marginal footprint of one 400-token Le Chat response (Mistral Large 2): 45 mL of water, 1.14 gCO2e, 0.16 mg Sb eq, excluding user devices. Lifecycle scope that includes electricity and hardware, so it is not comparable with on-site-only figures. Mistral calls it a rough estimate.

entries.label: Energy per average ChatGPT query (OpenAI CEO statement)
entries.source_title: Sam Altman: ChatGPT queries consume 0.34 watt-hours of electricity and 0.000085 gallons of water
entries.evidence: Altman states an average ChatGPT query uses about 0.34 Wh. Unverified, with no published methodology.

entries.label: Water per average ChatGPT query (OpenAI CEO statement)
entries.source_title: Sam Altman: ChatGPT queries consume 0.34 watt-hours of electricity and 0.000085 gallons of water
entries.evidence: Altman's blog post 'The Gentle Singularity' (June 2025) says an average query uses about 0.000085 gallons of water, roughly one fifteenth of a teaspoon (about 0.32 mL). No methodology, scope or definition of 'average query' was published.

entries.label: Water per medium-length GPT-3 response (UC Riverside, Making AI Less Thirsty)
entries.source_title: Making AI Less "Thirsty": Uncovering and Addressing the Secret Water Footprint of AI Models
entries.evidence: GPT-3 needs to consume a 500 mL bottle of water for roughly 10-50 medium-length responses, depending on when and where it is deployed (on-site cooling plus water behind the electricity). A modeled scenario, not a measurement; the authors call it conservative. Origin of the 'one bottle of water per query' claim, which misreads it as one bottle per response.
